scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. Your client was the developer, the joint venture ended, and it agreed to buy a flat instead. Can it still go to RERA?
On the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty six, a single bench of Honourable Justice P B Balaji of the Madras High Court answered that question.
scenes.shown: On 30 October 2026, a single bench of Honourable Justice P.B. Balaji of the Madras High Court answered that question.

scenes.dialogue: In twenty twelve, Bennett Property Holdings signed a joint venture agreement with land owners to develop their land. Later, by consent, it was terminated.
scenes.shown: In 2012, Bennett Property Holdings signed a joint venture agreement with land owners to develop their land. Later, by consent, it was terminated.

scenes.dialogue: Then the roles reversed. The land owners would build, and Bennett would buy an apartment, through an agreement of sale and a separate construction agreement.
Bennett says the land owners, now the builders, delayed construction and did not hand over possession. So it sought compensation before the Tamil Nadu RERA.
In July, citing the old joint venture, the Adjudicating Officer rejected it as a monetary deal, triable only by a Commercial Court.
The High Court held that Bennett is an allottee under Section Two of RERA. Buying its flat with an undivided share is not a commercial transaction.
scenes.shown: The High Court held that Bennett is an allottee under Section 2 of RERA. Buying its flat with an undivided share is not a commercial transaction.

scenes.dialogue: Once the joint venture ended, the parties became strangers, so that old deal cannot be used against the buyer. Land owners who turn developers are bound by RERA.
Calling the officer's finding perverse, the Court allowed the revision. If in order, the complaint must be numbered, the land owners heard, and decided on merits.
